eligibility_criteria: The SAT merit list is announced alongside the results of the IBA Aptitude Test.
The IBA system will evaluate the candidate’s placement on the merit list based on the higher of the two scores, provided at least one score meets the cut-off criteria for the chosen program.
✅ Eligibility Criteria: Must have domicile of Punjab Province .
Must have secured at least 60% marks (First Division) in Intermediate Annual Examination 2025.

Must have passed through a Punjab Board OR the Federal Board of Intermediate & Secondary Education (only students from federal institutions, private institutions, or private candidates within Punjab are eligible).
Eligible students are strongly encouraged to apply before the deadline.
test_pattern: Syllabus & Passing Threshold / Marks for the Written Test The aptitude test will consist of three parts (i) English Section (35%), (i) Mathematics Section (35%), and (iii) Specialized Section (30%).
English section will contain comprehension, grammar, composition, and vocabulary.

Mathematics section will test the knowledge of fundamental mathematics and will be in line with curriculum of SAT/GMAT, and Specialized section will contain the topics related to the subject positions.
There will be no negative marking in the test.
Aptitude Test will be held in Karachi only.
Candidates who under perform in the aptitude test and do not meet SHD prescribed criteria will not be called for Group Discussion.

The Entry Test will consist of two parts, English and Mathematics English An acceptable degree of proficiency in one of the languages of wider communication is a life-skill in the contemporary academic and professional environment.
The Reading Comprehension Section will assess comprehension at all the three levels; literal, inferential and critical.
scholarships: Must fulfill additional financial aid criteria prescribed by the Institution.
For further information, please contact the Financial Aid Office, IBA Karachi .
These need-based scholarships are funded through the Zakat and valuable support of public and private sector donors.

Upon submission of need-based scholarship form by student, the IBA facilitates by providing 'bridge financing' till the applicants are successfully connected with the Public or Private sector scholarship donor and Zakat funds.
The level of bridge financing is determined by the financial need of student which is assessed through the information provided in financial aid application form as submitted by student.
The repetition of courses for grade improvement or otherwise, and previously withdrawn courses or deficiency courses, are not covered under need-based scholarships.
The repetition of courses for grade improvement or previously withdrawn courses is not covered under need-based scholarships.
Scholarship awards are subject to the availability of funds and the Committee's approval.

hostel_info: The fees for the Summer Semester for Hostel residents who wish to stay during the summer for various reasons will be charged on prorate basis.
Two hostels, one each for female and male students, are located within the premises of the University of Karachi.
The hostels are spread over an area of 2.5 acres, surrounded by lush green lawns, trees, and gardens.
The design of the hostels amalgamates the needs of modern urban sustainable living, while vast and open corridors enable a pleasant and properly ventilated living space.
The IBA hostel life is a testimony to IBA’s diversity and inclusivity.
The IBA hostels provide an atmosphere where students can learn and develop life-long associations while enjoying a comfortable setting.
Residents’ security is a top priority for the institute and the hostels are guarded 24/7 by professional security personnel, with the entrance and exit points under constant CCTV surveillance.
